[Conservative](../codex/factions.md#conservative)

## Appearance

Anne is a girl with a slim, milk-white throat, delicate features, and a pointed freckled face. She possesses solemn gray eyes that are big, bright, and starry, alongside cheeks that can be faintly flushed with pink. She stands taller than [Miss Barry](../character/josephine-barry.md). Her hair is naturally red and often worn in long braids, though it is once described as streaming unbraided in a torrent of brightness, or as having a splendid [Titian](../character/titian.md) hue; at other times, it turns green and eventually has to be shingled closely.

## Personality

Anne is a highly imaginative and talkative girl who weaves optimism into her dreams of the future, though over time she grows noticeably quieter. She exhibits a sharp intelligence and obedience, being willing to work hard and quick to learn, though she can also be stubborn, heedless, impulsive, and tenacious when holding grudges. Intense in both her hatreds and her loves, she harbours a deep fear of walking through the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood) after dark. Mechanically and practically capable, she knows how to row a flat-bottomed dory, possesses a good singing voice, and knows how to treat croup with ipecac. Academically ambitious, she aims to become a teacher, resolve to win the Avery scholarship through hard work, and go to [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), desiring above all to pass high in her examinations for the sake of [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md).

## History

Born in [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke), [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), Anne was left an orphan at three months old after her mother died of fever. She spent her early childhood working in the households of Mrs. [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md) and Mrs. [Hammond](../character/hammond.md) before residing in an asylum for four months until Mrs. [Spencer](../character/spencer.md) brought her to Prince [Edward Island](../codex/places.md#edward-island). Upon arriving at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), she learned that the [Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) siblings had requested a boy, though [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) eventually agreed to let her stay. Anne quickly made a soulmate in her neighbor [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), despite temporarily losing access to her after accidentally serving [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) currant wine. During her school days, Anne held a fierce academic rivalry with [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), which began after she smashed a slate over his head for calling her 'Carrots.' [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) showed his deep fondness for Anne by surprising her with a trendy dress with puffed sleeves for a school concert. Anne proved her academic talent by tying for first place on the Island's entrance examinations, earning her a spot at Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) where she subsequently won the prestigious Avery scholarship. However, following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack and news that [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) was losing her eyesight, Anne gave up her scholarship to stay at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Learning that [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) had yielded the local teaching position to her, Anne forgave him for past grievances and formed a close friendship with him.

## Quotes

> "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P24](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0024)

> “I think he’s lovely,” said Anne reproachfully. “He is so very sympathetic. He didn’t mind how much I talked—he seemed to like it. I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.”
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P26](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0026)

> "Oh, I don’t mean that sort of a name. I mean just a name you gave it yourself. Didn’t you give it a name? May I give it one then? May I call it—let me see—Bonny would do—may I call it Bonny while I’m here? Oh, do let me!"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P33](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0033)

> "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P11](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0011)

> "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P43](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0043)

## Relationships

### [Allan](../character/allan.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/allan--anne-shirley.md)

Mrs. Allan is Avonlea's minister's wife and Anne's Sunday school teacher, becoming a valued friend and mentor who acts as a extra conscience. Despite early embarrassment when Anne accidentally serves her a cake flavored with liniment, Mrs. Allan responds with kindness and comforts her. Anne continues to seek her out in difficult times, speaking with her about finding moments of joy amidst deep sorrow after Matthew's death.

### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--diana-barry.md)

[Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) is Anne's closest schoolmate and devoted bosom friend. The two swear an eternal friendship upon their first meeting in the [Barry](../character/barry.md) garden, standing by each other through school hardships and childhood play. Their bond is deeply cemented when Anne stays up all night to successfully save Diana's little sister from severe croup.

### [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Anne's dynamic with [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) begins with intense hostility after he taunts her by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash a slate over his head and reject his apology. They become fierce academic rivals competing for the top of their class, even though [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) harbors romantic feelings for her, saves her from drowning when a boat re-enactment goes wrong, and keeps a rose she dropped. Eventually, their long-standing antagonism softens, and they reconcile to become close friends who help each other with their studies.

### [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

[Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) takes Anne into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) despite initial shock and reluctance over expecting a boy. She serves as a strict guardian and teacher to Anne, attempting to instil practical discipline, religious manners, and proper behavior. Over time, their relationship evolves into a deep, loving bond as [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) grows deeply fond of Anne and privately grieves the passage of her childhood.

### [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--matthew-cuthbert.md)

[Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) is Anne's gentlest champion and dearest friend at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) from the moment he brings her home. He consistently advocates for her to stay, supports her imaginative nature, and offers quiet, steady encouragement throughout her school endeavors. His sudden death leaves Anne deeply heartbroken, though she cherishes the loving bond they shared.
